是否需要限定医学影像模态或解剖部位（如CT、MRI、特定器官）？

claims.text: 现有证据仅来自若干摘要，且各研究的分割任务、影像模态与评估设置不同，无法据此给出MedSAM与nnU-Net的普遍性优劣结论；只能按具体任务分别描述两者差异。
limitations: 所有证据均为摘要层面，未提供全文方法细节
检索为部分结果，不能据此判断文献整体情况

claims.text: 在CT骨转移瘤2D切片分割中，nnU-Net的Dice为0.6849、归一化Hausdorff距离为0.0473，优于无提示MedSAM适配版的Dice 0.6280与NHD 0.1008；作者据此认为nnU-Net是稳健的强基线。
limitations: 单一数据集（88例患者），仅摘要报告
MedSAM为无提示适配版，非其全部使用方式

claims.text: 在心脏磁共振弹性成像的左心室心肌分割中，最佳nnU-Net（全平均归一化幅值图像）Dice为0.82±0.04，最佳MedSAM（半自动微调加强ROI平滑）Dice为0.82±0.02，两者均达到阅片者间一致性水平；但全自动MedSAM变体较低（autoprompt 0.68±0.09，box regression 0.71±0.08）。
limitations: 仅16名健康男性志愿者，样本小
MedSAM最佳结果依赖半自动与强ROI平滑，与nnU-Net的全自动流程不完全对等

claims.text: 在原发性中枢神经系统淋巴瘤（临床常规增强T1 MRI）及MSD-BraTS胶质瘤分割中，监督学习（nnU-Net）在两个数据集上均以较大幅度显著优于包括MedSAM在内的分割基础模型，作者认为任务专用模型仍不可替代。
limitations: 摘要未给出具体Dice数值与统计细节

claims.text: 在神经肌肉疾病患者大腿MR的多类肌肉分割中，微调SAM的编码器/解码器配置在Moderate与Severe组略优于3D nnU-Net（DSC 0.886 vs 0.883、0.857 vs 0.850），Early组相当（0.925）；MedSAM未表现出相对SAM的优势，该摘要未报告MedSAM与nnU-Net的直接数值对比。
limitations: MedSAM与nnU-Net的直接比较数值未在摘要中给出

claims.text: 在BraTS 2023胶质瘤数据上，给予极精确的边界框提示时SAM/SAM 2的Dice可达约0.89并超过nnU-Net，但作者指出实际中难以提供如此精确的提示，因此nnU-Net仍是主导的医学分割网络；微调后MedSAM等的点提示性能提升明显，但仍不及边界框提示或nnU-Net。
limitations: 摘要未给出MedSAM与nnU-Net的具体Dice数值
结论依赖提示质量设定

claims.text: 综合上述摘要，两者的差异主要体现在使用范式而非单一精度：nnU-Net为任务专用、全自动的自配置监督框架，在多数报告任务中作为强基线或占优；MedSAM为提示/基础模型，其表现高度依赖提示质量、是否微调及自动化程度（零样本、半自动、全自动变体差异明显）。
limitations: 该概括基于不同任务与不同评估设置的摘要，非头对头汇总分析
未涉及训练数据需求、推理效率等维度的直接证据

claims.text: 关于训练数据规模需求、推理速度/计算成本以及跨模态泛化能力的定量差异，所提供摘要中未找到直接比较数据。
limitations: 仅基于所提供摘要，不能推断这些维度在文献中无相关研究

openalex_record.title: Comparison of Foundation Models MedSAM and DINOv3 with the nnU-Net Framework for Bone Metastasis Segmentation in Computed Tomography Scans
openalex_record.abstract: This study compares three methods for 2D bone metastasis segmentation on computed tomography slices-the self-configuring nnU-Net pipeline, a fine-tuned DINOv3 foundation model, and a prompt-free MedSAM foundation model adaptation-to assess their suitability for clinical-grade lesion delineation. Methods: A dataset of 2D CT slices from 88 patients (11,006 image–label pairs) was annotated by experts. The three models were trained and evaluated under comparable conditions, using model-specific native input resolutions and training schedules. Performance was evaluated using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Normalized Hausdorff distance (NHD) on a held-out test set, with a separate cohort of previously unseen patients. On a held-out test set, the MedSAM, DINOv3, and nnU-Net models achieved the following Dice scores: 0.6280, 0.4480, and 0.6849, respectively. Additionally, on a held-out test set, the MedSAM, DINOv3, and nnU-Net models achieved the following normalized Hausdorff distances: 0.1008, 0.1019, and 0.0473, respectively. In conclusion, the nnU-Net framework provides robust segmentation performance and serves as a strong baseline for 2D slice-wise bone metastasis delineation even with limited annotated data.

sources.title: Comparison of Foundation Models MedSAM and DINOv3 with the nnU-Net Framework for Bone Metastasis Segmentation in Computed Tomography Scans

evidence.text: This study compares three methods for 2D bone metastasis segmentation on computed tomography slices-the self-configuring nnU-Net pipeline, a fine-tuned DINOv3 foundation model, and a prompt-free MedSAM foundation model adaptation-to assess their suitability for clinical-grade lesion delineation. Methods: A dataset of 2D CT slices from 88 patients (11,006 image–label pairs) was annotated by experts. The three models were trained and evaluated under comparable conditions, using model-specific native input resolutions and training schedules. Performance was evaluated using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Normalized Hausdorff distance (NHD) on a held-out test set, with a separate cohort of previously unseen patients. On a held-out test set, the MedSAM, DINOv3, and nnU-Net models achieved the following Dice scores: 0.6280, 0.4480, and 0.6849, respectively. Additionally, on a held-out test set, the MedSAM, DINOv3, and nnU-Net models achieved the following normalized Hausdorff distances: 0.1008, 0.1019, and 0.0473, respectively. In conclusion, the nnU-Net framework provides robust segmentation performance and serves as a strong baseline for 2D slice-wise bone metastasis delineation even with limited annotated data.

openalex_record.title: Toward self-contained cardiac magnetic resonance elastography: Deep learning-based segmentation of the left ventricular myocardium
openalex_record.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) is an emerging modality for noninvasive assessment of left ventricular (LV) myocardial stiffness. Accurate LV myocardium delineation is essential for MRE analysis, yet current workflows often rely on manual annotation and additional structural MRI. It remains uncertain whether native cardiac MRE data alone are sufficient for reliable automated LV segmentation. PURPOSE: To evaluate deep learning approaches for LV myocardium segmentation on cardiac MRE data and to assess the influence of input representation and automation strategy on segmentation performance. METHODS: Cardiac MRE data from 16 healthy male volunteers were used to train and evaluate two contemporary segmentation frameworks, nnU-Net v2 and MedSAM. Reader 1 annotated the full dataset using MRE magnitude images, and Reader 2 independently annotated the test set, enabling model performance to be benchmarked against inter-reader agreement. nnU-Net was trained using multiple input representations and training strategies. MedSAM was evaluated in zero-shot, semi-automated, fine-tuned, autoprompt, and box-regression configurations. RESULTS: Inter-reader Dice agreement was 0.79 ± 0.03. The best nnU-Net model, trained on fully averaged normalized magnitude images, achieved a Dice score of 0.82 ± 0.04. Performance was lower with magnitude-plus-phase and real-plus-imaginary inputs, with Dice scores of 0.65 ± 0.21 and 0.60 ± 0.20, respectively, and also decreased with non-normalized magnitude input, which yielded a Dice score of 0.75 ± 0.05. The best MedSAM result was obtained with a semi-automated fine-tuned variant using strong ROI smoothing, which achieved a Dice score of 0.82 ± 0.02. Fully automated MedSAM variants performed less well, with Dice scores of 0.68 ± 0.09 for autoprompt and 0.71 ± 0.08 for box regression. CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac MRE data alone demonstrated the feasibility of accurate LV myocardium segmentation, with nnU-Net and MedSAM both reaching inter-reader-level performance. These findings support direct segmentation of the LV myocardium from native cardiac MRE and represent a step toward a self-contained cardiac MRE workflow.

sources.title: Toward self-contained cardiac magnetic resonance elastography: Deep learning-based segmentation of the left ventricular myocardium

evidence.text: BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) is an emerging modality for noninvasive assessment of left ventricular (LV) myocardial stiffness. Accurate LV myocardium delineation is essential for MRE analysis, yet current workflows often rely on manual annotation and additional structural MRI. It remains uncertain whether native cardiac MRE data alone are sufficient for reliable automated LV segmentation. PURPOSE: To evaluate deep learning approaches for LV myocardium segmentation on cardiac MRE data and to assess the influence of input representation and automation strategy on segmentation performance. METHODS: Cardiac MRE data from 16 healthy male volunteers were used to train and evaluate two contemporary segmentation frameworks, nnU-Net v2 and MedSAM. Reader 1 annotated the full dataset using MRE magnitude images, and Reader 2 independently annotated the test set, enabling model performance to be benchmarked against inter-reader agreement. nnU-Net was trained using multiple input representations and training strategies. MedSAM was evaluated in zero-shot, semi-automated, fine-tuned, autoprompt, and box-regression configurations. RESULTS: Inter-reader Dice agreement was 0.79 ± 0.03. The best nnU-Net model, trained on fully averaged normalized magnitude images, achieved a Dice score of 0.82 ± 0.04. Performance was lower with magnitude-plus-phase and real-plus-imaginary inputs, with Dice scores of 0.65 ± 0.21 and 0.60 ± 0.20, respectively, and also decreased with non-normalized magnitude input, which yielded a Dice score of 0.75 ± 0.05. The best MedSAM result was obtained with a semi-automated fine-tuned variant using strong ROI smoothing, which achieved a Dice score of 0.82 ± 0.02. Fully automated MedSAM variants performed less well, with Dice scores of 0.68 ± 0.09 for autoprompt and 0.71 ± 0.08 for box regression. CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac MRE data alone demonstrated the feasibility of accurate LV myocardium segmentation, with nnU-Net and MedSAM both reaching inter-reader-level performance. These findings support direct segmentation of the LV myocardium from native cardiac MRE and represent a step toward a self-contained cardiac MRE workflow.

openalex_record.title: Comparing foundation models and nnU-Net for segmentation of primary brain lymphoma on clinical routine post-contrast T1-weighted MRI
openalex_record.journal: SPIE Medical Imaging: Clinical and Biomedical Imaging
openalex_record.abstract: Primary Central Nervous System (PCNS) lymphoma is an aggressive brain tumor, and MRI segmentation is crucial for diagnosis and follow-up. Segmentation foundation models (FM) offer an alternative to classical supervised deep learning. This paper evaluates the performance of segmentation foundation models (FMs), including Segment Anything Model (SAM), MedSAM, and UniverSeg, against traditional supervised learning (with nnU-net) for lymphoma segmentation using clinical routine data and for glioma segmentation using the public dataset MSD-BraTS. Results showed that supervised learning outperformed FMs significantly by vast margins on both datasets. Task-specific models like nnU-net remain essential for complex segmentation tasks.

sources.title: Comparing foundation models and nnU-Net for segmentation of primary brain lymphoma on clinical routine post-contrast T1-weighted MRI
sources.journal: SPIE Medical Imaging: Clinical and Biomedical Imaging

evidence.text: Primary Central Nervous System (PCNS) lymphoma is an aggressive brain tumor, and MRI segmentation is crucial for diagnosis and follow-up. Segmentation foundation models (FM) offer an alternative to classical supervised deep learning. This paper evaluates the performance of segmentation foundation models (FMs), including Segment Anything Model (SAM), MedSAM, and UniverSeg, against traditional supervised learning (with nnU-net) for lymphoma segmentation using clinical routine data and for glioma segmentation using the public dataset MSD-BraTS. Results showed that supervised learning outperformed FMs significantly by vast margins on both datasets. Task-specific models like nnU-net remain essential for complex segmentation tasks.

openalex_record.title: Exploring foundation models for multi-class muscle segmentation in MR images of neuromuscular disorders: A comparative analysis of accuracy and uncertainty
openalex_record.journal: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine
openalex_record.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Deep learning (DL) models have shown promise for skeletal muscle (SM) segmentation in MR images, which is crucial for extracting biomarkers in neuromuscular disorders (NMDs). However, to ensure safe clinical use, models should provide uncertainty estimates, allowing radiologists to assess predictions and intervene when needed. Foundation Models (FMs) have the potential to play a significant role due to their strong generalization capabilities and well-calibrated predictions. However, their applicability in this context has not yet been explored. This study aims to develop an accurate and trustworthy technique by fine-tuning FMs to delineate fatty-infiltrated SM fascicles in NMD patients. METHODS: We fine-tuned Segment Anything Model (SAM) and MedSAM using two configurations - encoder/decoder and decoder only - and compared their performance against state-of-the-art 2D and 3D nnU-Net using a dataset of thigh MR images from 76 NMD patients, categorized into Early, Moderate, and Severe fatty infiltration groups. Accuracy was evaluated using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), while Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) was evaluated using the Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and the Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL). Deep Ensembles were used to convey epistemic uncertainty in addition to the aleatoric counterpart. RESULTS: SAM's fine-tuned encoder/decoder outperformed nnU-Net 3D in Moderate and Severe cases (DSC: 0.886 vs 0.883 and 0.857 vs 0.850) and was comparable in Early (DSC: 0.925). MedSAM did not show an advantage over SAM. Regarding UQ, SAM exhibited superior calibration in Moderate and Severe groups (ECE: 3.6% vs. 5.1% and 3.3% vs. 7.1%), CONCLUSIONS:: In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that fine-tuning SAM yields superior performance, considering both accuracy and UQ metrics, highlighting its enhanced reliability in challenging NMD imaging scenarios.

sources.title: Exploring foundation models for multi-class muscle segmentation in MR images of neuromuscular disorders: A comparative analysis of accuracy and uncertainty
sources.journal: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine

evidence.text: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Deep learning (DL) models have shown promise for skeletal muscle (SM) segmentation in MR images, which is crucial for extracting biomarkers in neuromuscular disorders (NMDs). However, to ensure safe clinical use, models should provide uncertainty estimates, allowing radiologists to assess predictions and intervene when needed. Foundation Models (FMs) have the potential to play a significant role due to their strong generalization capabilities and well-calibrated predictions. However, their applicability in this context has not yet been explored. This study aims to develop an accurate and trustworthy technique by fine-tuning FMs to delineate fatty-infiltrated SM fascicles in NMD patients. METHODS: We fine-tuned Segment Anything Model (SAM) and MedSAM using two configurations - encoder/decoder and decoder only - and compared their performance against state-of-the-art 2D and 3D nnU-Net using a dataset of thigh MR images from 76 NMD patients, categorized into Early, Moderate, and Severe fatty infiltration groups. Accuracy was evaluated using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), while Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) was evaluated using the Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and the Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL). Deep Ensembles were used to convey epistemic uncertainty in addition to the aleatoric counterpart. RESULTS: SAM's fine-tuned encoder/decoder outperformed nnU-Net 3D in Moderate and Severe cases (DSC: 0.886 vs 0.883 and 0.857 vs 0.850) and was comparable in Early (DSC: 0.925). MedSAM did not show an advantage over SAM. Regarding UQ, SAM exhibited superior calibration in Moderate and Severe groups (ECE: 3.6% vs. 5.1% and 3.3% vs. 7.1%), CONCLUSIONS:: In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that fine-tuning SAM yields superior performance, considering both accuracy and UQ metrics, highlighting its enhanced reliability in challenging NMD imaging scenarios.

openalex_record.abstract: Medical image segmentation has greatly aided medical diagnosis, with U-Net based architectures and nnU-Net providing state-of-the-art performance. There have been numerous general promptable models and medical variations introduced in recent years, but there is currently a lack of evaluation and comparison of these models across a variety of prompt qualities on a common medical dataset. This research uses Segment Anything Model (SAM), Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), MedSAM, SAM-Med-3D, and nnU-Net to obtain zero-shot inference on the BraTS 2023 adult glioma and pediatrics dataset across multiple prompt qualities for both points and bounding boxes. Several of these models exhibit promising Dice scores, particularly SAM and SAM 2 achieving scores of up to 0.894 and 0.893, respectively when given extremely accurate bounding box prompts which exceeds nnU-Net's segmentation performance. However, nnU-Net remains the dominant medical image segmentation network due to the impracticality of providing highly accurate prompts to the models. The model and prompt evaluation, as well as the comparison, are extended through fine-tuning SAM, SAM 2, MedSAM, and SAM-Med-3D on the pediatrics dataset. The improvements in point prompt performance after fine-tuning are substantial and show promise for future investigation, but are unable to achieve better segmentation than bounding boxes or nnU-Net.

evidence.text: Medical image segmentation has greatly aided medical diagnosis, with U-Net based architectures and nnU-Net providing state-of-the-art performance. There have been numerous general promptable models and medical variations introduced in recent years, but there is currently a lack of evaluation and comparison of these models across a variety of prompt qualities on a common medical dataset. This research uses Segment Anything Model (SAM), Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), MedSAM, SAM-Med-3D, and nnU-Net to obtain zero-shot inference on the BraTS 2023 adult glioma and pediatrics dataset across multiple prompt qualities for both points and bounding boxes. Several of these models exhibit promising Dice scores, particularly SAM and SAM 2 achieving scores of up to 0.894 and 0.893, respectively when given extremely accurate bounding box prompts which exceeds nnU-Net's segmentation performance. However, nnU-Net remains the dominant medical image segmentation network due to the impracticality of providing highly accurate prompts to the models. The model and prompt evaluation, as well as the comparison, are extended through fine-tuning SAM, SAM 2, MedSAM, and SAM-Med-3D on the pediatrics dataset. The improvements in point prompt performance after fine-tuning are substantial and show promise for future investigation, but are unable to achieve better segmentation than bounding boxes or nnU-Net.

records.title: Comparing foundation models and nnU-Net for segmentation of primary brain lymphoma on clinical routine post-contrast T1-weighted MRI
records.journal: SPIE Medical Imaging: Clinical and Biomedical Imaging
records.abstract: Primary Central Nervous System (PCNS) lymphoma is an aggressive brain tumor, and MRI segmentation is crucial for diagnosis and follow-up. Segmentation foundation models (FM) offer an alternative to classical supervised deep learning. This paper evaluates the performance of segmentation foundation models (FMs), including Segment Anything Model (SAM), MedSAM, and UniverSeg, against traditional supervised learning (with nnU-net) for lymphoma segmentation using clinical routine data and for glioma segmentation using the public dataset MSD-BraTS. Results showed that supervised learning outperformed FMs significantly by vast margins on both datasets. Task-specific models like nnU-net remain essential for complex segmentation tasks.

records.title: Comparison of Foundation Models MedSAM and DINOv3 with the nnU-Net Framework for Bone Metastasis Segmentation in Computed Tomography Scans
records.abstract: This study compares three methods for 2D bone metastasis segmentation on computed tomography slices-the self-configuring nnU-Net pipeline, a fine-tuned DINOv3 foundation model, and a prompt-free MedSAM foundation model adaptation-to assess their suitability for clinical-grade lesion delineation. Methods: A dataset of 2D CT slices from 88 patients (11,006 image–label pairs) was annotated by experts. The three models were trained and evaluated under comparable conditions, using model-specific native input resolutions and training schedules. Performance was evaluated using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Normalized Hausdorff distance (NHD) on a held-out test set, with a separate cohort of previously unseen patients. On a held-out test set, the MedSAM, DINOv3, and nnU-Net models achieved the following Dice scores: 0.6280, 0.4480, and 0.6849, respectively. Additionally, on a held-out test set, the MedSAM, DINOv3, and nnU-Net models achieved the following normalized Hausdorff distances: 0.1008, 0.1019, and 0.0473, respectively. In conclusion, the nnU-Net framework provides robust segmentation performance and serves as a strong baseline for 2D slice-wise bone metastasis delineation even with limited annotated data.

records.title: Necessity and impact of specialization of large foundation model for medical segmentation tasks
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Large foundation models, such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM), have shown remarkable performance in image segmentation tasks. However, the optimal approach to achieve true utility of these models for domain-specific applications, such as medical image segmentation, remains an open question. Recent studies have released a medical version of the foundation model MedSAM by training on vast medical data, who promised SOTA medical segmentation. Independent community inspection and dissection is needed. PURPOSE: Foundation models are developed for general purposes. On the other hand, stable delivery of reliable performance is key to clinical utility. This study aims at elucidating the potential advantage and limitations of landing the foundation models in clinical use by assessing the performance of off-the-shelf medical foundation model MedSAM for the segmentation of anatomical structures in pelvic MR images. We also explore the simple remedies by evaluating the dependency on prompting scheme. Finally, we demonstrate the need and performance gain of further specialized fine-tuning. METHODS: MedSAM and its lightweight version LiteMedSAM were evaluated out-of-the-box on a public MR dataset consisting of 589 pelvic images split 80:20 for training and testing. An nnU-Net model was trained from scratch to serve as a benchmark and to provide bounding box prompts for MedSAM. MedSAM was evaluated using different quality bounding boxes, those derived from ground truth labels, those derived from nnU-Net, and those derived from the former two but with 5-pixel isometric expansion. Lastly, LiteMedSAM was refined on the training set and reevaluated on this task. RESULTS: Out-of-the-box MedSAM and LiteMedSAM both performed poorly across the structure set, especially for disjoint or non-convex structures. Varying prompt with different bounding box inputs had minimal effect. For example, the mean Dice score and mean Hausdorff distances (in mm) for obturator internus using MedSAM and LiteMedSAM were {0.251 ± 0.110, 0.101 ± 0.079} and {34.142 ± 5.196, 33.688 ± 5.306}, respectively. Fine-tuning of LiteMedSAM led to significant performance gain, improving Dice score and Hausdorff distance for the obturator internus to 0.864 ± 0.123 and 5.022 ± 10.684, on par with nnU-Net with no significant difference in evaluation of most structures. All segmentation structures benefited significantly from specialized refinement, at varying improvement margin. CONCLUSION: While our study alludes to the potential of deep learning models like MedSAM and LiteMedSAM for medical segmentation, it highlights the need for specialized refinement and adjudication. Off-the-shelf use of such large foundation models is highly likely to be suboptimal, and specialized fine-tuning is often necessary to achieve clinical desired accuracy and stability.

records.title: Toward self-contained cardiac magnetic resonance elastography: Deep learning-based segmentation of the left ventricular myocardium
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) is an emerging modality for noninvasive assessment of left ventricular (LV) myocardial stiffness. Accurate LV myocardium delineation is essential for MRE analysis, yet current workflows often rely on manual annotation and additional structural MRI. It remains uncertain whether native cardiac MRE data alone are sufficient for reliable automated LV segmentation. PURPOSE: To evaluate deep learning approaches for LV myocardium segmentation on cardiac MRE data and to assess the influence of input representation and automation strategy on segmentation performance. METHODS: Cardiac MRE data from 16 healthy male volunteers were used to train and evaluate two contemporary segmentation frameworks, nnU-Net v2 and MedSAM. Reader 1 annotated the full dataset using MRE magnitude images, and Reader 2 independently annotated the test set, enabling model performance to be benchmarked against inter-reader agreement. nnU-Net was trained using multiple input representations and training strategies. MedSAM was evaluated in zero-shot, semi-automated, fine-tuned, autoprompt, and box-regression configurations. RESULTS: Inter-reader Dice agreement was 0.79 ± 0.03. The best nnU-Net model, trained on fully averaged normalized magnitude images, achieved a Dice score of 0.82 ± 0.04. Performance was lower with magnitude-plus-phase and real-plus-imaginary inputs, with Dice scores of 0.65 ± 0.21 and 0.60 ± 0.20, respectively, and also decreased with non-normalized magnitude input, which yielded a Dice score of 0.75 ± 0.05. The best MedSAM result was obtained with a semi-automated fine-tuned variant using strong ROI smoothing, which achieved a Dice score of 0.82 ± 0.02. Fully automated MedSAM variants performed less well, with Dice scores of 0.68 ± 0.09 for autoprompt and 0.71 ± 0.08 for box regression. CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac MRE data alone demonstrated the feasibility of accurate LV myocardium segmentation, with nnU-Net and MedSAM both reaching inter-reader-level performance. These findings support direct segmentation of the LV myocardium from native cardiac MRE and represent a step toward a self-contained cardiac MRE workflow.

records.title: AI-Driven MRI-based Brain Tumour Segmentation Benchmarking
records.abstract: Medical image segmentation has greatly aided medical diagnosis, with U-Net based architectures and nnU-Net providing state-of-the-art performance. There have been numerous general promptable models and medical variations introduced in recent years, but there is currently a lack of evaluation and comparison of these models across a variety of prompt qualities on a common medical dataset. This research uses Segment Anything Model (SAM), Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), MedSAM, SAM-Med-3D, and nnU-Net to obtain zero-shot inference on the BraTS 2023 adult glioma and pediatrics dataset across multiple prompt qualities for both points and bounding boxes. Several of these models exhibit promising Dice scores, particularly SAM and SAM 2 achieving scores of up to 0.894 and 0.893, respectively when given extremely accurate bounding box prompts which exceeds nnU-Net's segmentation performance. However, nnU-Net remains the dominant medical image segmentation network due to the impracticality of providing highly accurate prompts to the models. The model and prompt evaluation, as well as the comparison, are extended through fine-tuning SAM, SAM 2, MedSAM, and SAM-Med-3D on the pediatrics dataset. The improvements in point prompt performance after fine-tuning are substantial and show promise for future investigation, but are unable to achieve better segmentation than bounding boxes or nnU-Net.

records.title: Integrating self-configuring and foundational deep learning segmentation models for identifying the anal sphincter complex and perianal fistulae on pelvic MRI
records.journal: SPIE Medical Imaging: Image-Guided Procedures, Robotic Interventions, and Modeling
records.abstract: Perianal fistulas remain one of the most common complications associated with Crohn’s disease, with an urgent need for improved interventional guidance and surgical planning. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is routinely used for noninvasive imaging assessment of perianal fistulizing Crohn’s Disease (CD-PAF), but suffers from significant inter-reader variability in accurately determining fistula tracts vis a vis anorectal anatomy. Towards overcoming these issues, we present a novel approach which integrates self-configuring segmentation frameworks (nnU-net) with generalized foundation models (MedSAM) toward the task of automated segmentation of fistula tracts and as well as internal and external sphincter muscles on pelvic MRI. We utilized a cohort comprising both baseline and follow-up MRI scans from 92 CD-PAF patients, for which manual annotations of all three anorectal structures were available. In hold-out validation, the integrated MedSAM-nnUnet model yielded the best overall performance in segmenting out the internal (Dice of 0.96 ± 0.18) and external sphincter muscles (Dice of 0.59 ± 0.09), as well as perianal fistulae (Dice of 0.55 ± 0.09); which represented significant improvements over MedSAM and nnU-net models individually. Integrating foundation with self-configuring segmentation models offers a novel automated annotation approach for detailed visualization of anorectal anatomy to guide surgical interventions in CD-PAF patients.

records.title: NodulePrompt: Prompt-Guided Segmentation of Infectious Pulmonary Nodules
records.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: First public release of NodulePrompt, the code accompanying our work on prompt-guided segmentation of infectious pulmonary nodules. It includes: MedSAM zero-shot and MedSAM+LoRA adapters; crop-guided and prompt-matched nnU-Net export; dense box-prior QA; the preprocessing used in the paper; Dice, HD95, ASSD and case-level bootstrap evaluation; the fixed paper configuration and a synthetic example. The release was checked from a clean GitHub installation, then tested with MedSAM on one real CT case. The nnU-Net dataset integrity check and preprocessing also passed for both 2d and 3d_fullres, with NoNormalization correctly applied to the box-prior channel. The clinical cohort and frozen splits cannot be released because of patient privacy and institutional restrictions.

records.title: PD05.07. Enhancing SAM-Med3D with Prototype-Contrast Boundary Optimization for Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Segmentation
records.abstract: Abstract Topic Esophageal Cancer: Other Background Precise segmentation of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) lesions on CT imaging is essential for treatment planning. While the Segment Anything Model for 3D medical images (SAM-Med3D) shows promise, its performance in delineating tumor boundaries remains suboptimal. We propose a prototype-contrast boundary optimization strategy to enhance segmentation accuracy. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, CT volumetric data from 310 ESCC patients who underwent esophagectomy were collected from two centers (Center A: n=161, July 2018–February 2023; Center B: n=149). Data from Center A were used for training and internal validation, while Center B served as the external testing cohort. We evaluated SAM-Med3D for ESCC lesion segmentation and compared it with state-of-the-art methods including nnU-Net, SegVol, and MedSAM. To address SAM-Med3D’s limitation in boundary delineation, we introduced a prototype-contrast boundary pixel clustering optimization. This approach employs contrastive learning to refine boundary pixel classification by pulling features toward correct class prototypes while pushing them away from incorrect ones. Performance was assessed using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and 95th percentile Hausdorff Distance (HD95). Results The optimized SAM-Med3D achieved a DSC of 76.23% on internal validation and 73.57% on external testing, representing a 3.11% improvement over the original SAM-Med3D (internal DSC: 73.12%; external DSC: 70.46%). Our method outperformed all baseline approaches: nnU-Net (internal/external DSC: 72.45%/69.18%), SegVol (70.83%/67.52%), and MedSAM (71.26%/68.34%). The optimized model also achieved the lowest HD95 values (internal: 6.48 mm; external: 7.81 mm), indicating superior boundary delineation accuracy. The performance advantage was consistent across both centers, demonstrating robust generalizability. Conclusion The prototype-contrast boundary pixel clustering optimization effectively enhances SAM-Med3D’s capability for ESCC lesion segmentation, achieving superior performance over nnU-Net, SegVol, and MedSAM across multicenter datasets. This approach addresses the critical challenge of accurate tumor boundary delineation and demonstrates strong generalizability, providing a valuable tool for preoperative assessment and surgical planning in ESCC.

records.title: A multi-paradigm evaluation spanning pixels to voxels for deep learning-based kidney tumor segmentation
records.abstract: Automated segmentation of kidney tumors from computed tomography (CT) scans is crit- ical for diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of renal cell carcinoma (RCC). While recent deep learning models report high Dice scores (>0.97), their clinical utility remains questionable due to false positive predictions that misclassify healthy tissue as tumors and computational constraints limiting real-world deployment. Unlike existing studies that emphasise quantitative metrics, this work investigates the critical gap between high segmentation accuracy and clinical applicability. We systematically evaluate six diverse architectures spanning 2D CNNs (U-Net, MedSAM) to 3D volumetric models (nnU-Net, UNETR, Total Segmenta- tor, MIScnn) on the KiTS19 dataset, emphasising false positive analysis, boundary delineation accuracy, and computational feasibility. Key findings [1]: MONAI U-Net achieves Dice score of 0.98 but exhibits excessive false positives, undermining clinical trust [2]; nnU-Net provides balanced performance (Dice: 0.82) with consistent results but demands 16GB VRAM [3]; MedSAM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy (Dice: 0.99) with minimal false positives but re- quires high-end GPUs [4]; computational constraints prevented full training of UNETR. This study identifies that high Dice scores do not guarantee clinical utility and provides actionable insights for developing clinically feasible segmentation tools for renal oncology applications including treatment planning, longitudinal monitoring, and risk assessment.

records.title: Exploring foundation models for multi-class muscle segmentation in MR images of neuromuscular disorders: A comparative analysis of accuracy and uncertainty
records.journal: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine
records.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Deep learning (DL) models have shown promise for skeletal muscle (SM) segmentation in MR images, which is crucial for extracting biomarkers in neuromuscular disorders (NMDs). However, to ensure safe clinical use, models should provide uncertainty estimates, allowing radiologists to assess predictions and intervene when needed. Foundation Models (FMs) have the potential to play a significant role due to their strong generalization capabilities and well-calibrated predictions. However, their applicability in this context has not yet been explored. This study aims to develop an accurate and trustworthy technique by fine-tuning FMs to delineate fatty-infiltrated SM fascicles in NMD patients. METHODS: We fine-tuned Segment Anything Model (SAM) and MedSAM using two configurations - encoder/decoder and decoder only - and compared their performance against state-of-the-art 2D and 3D nnU-Net using a dataset of thigh MR images from 76 NMD patients, categorized into Early, Moderate, and Severe fatty infiltration groups. Accuracy was evaluated using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), while Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) was evaluated using the Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and the Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL). Deep Ensembles were used to convey epistemic uncertainty in addition to the aleatoric counterpart. RESULTS: SAM's fine-tuned encoder/decoder outperformed nnU-Net 3D in Moderate and Severe cases (DSC: 0.886 vs 0.883 and 0.857 vs 0.850) and was comparable in Early (DSC: 0.925). MedSAM did not show an advantage over SAM. Regarding UQ, SAM exhibited superior calibration in Moderate and Severe groups (ECE: 3.6% vs. 5.1% and 3.3% vs. 7.1%), CONCLUSIONS:: In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that fine-tuning SAM yields superior performance, considering both accuracy and UQ metrics, highlighting its enhanced reliability in challenging NMD imaging scenarios.

records.title: Application of a Fusion Model Combining MRI-VASARI Features and ADC in Predicting the Molecular Subtypes of Adult-type Diffuse Gliomas
records.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
records.abstract: Objective: To develop a machine learning model integrating MRI visually accessible Rembrandt images (VASARI) features and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) parameters for the preoperative classification of the three subtypes of adult-type diffuse glioma. Methods: This study retrospectively enrolled 206 patients with pathologically confirmed adult-type diffuse glioma and divided them by scanner type into a training set (n=114) and an independent validation set (n=92). Tumor multi-region segmentation was conducted using nnU-Net, followed by extraction of VASARI features and ADC-related parameters. Recursive feature elimination with cross-validation (RFECV), XGBoost feature importance ranking, and incremental feature selection were applied to identify the optimal feature subset, and an XGBoost-based multiclass fusion model was subsequently constructed. Results: Twelve VASARI features and four ADC parameters (ADCmin, ADCmean, rADCmin, and rADCmean) differed significantly among the three subtypes. Eight features were finally selected for model construction. The fusion model achieved accuracies of 96.49% in the training set and 80.43% in the validation set. In the validation cohort, the area under the curves (AUCs) for predicting astrocytoma and glioblastoma were 0.96 and 0.97, respectively, both higher than those of the standalone VASARI and ADC models, while the AUC for oligodendroglioma was 0.59. SHAP analysis revealed that diffusion restriction, ADC parameters, and the margin of the non-enhancing region were the primary contributors to the model. Conclusion: The XGBoost-based fusion model integrating MRI-VASARI features and ADC demonstrated a high diagnostic performance in distinguishing glioblastoma and astrocytoma, but its ability to differentiate oligodendroglioma remained limited. Future studies should incorporate additional imaging features, such as calcification, to further improve the model performance.

records.title: A multi-task learning-based network for detecting three-dimensional osteometric landmarks of the shoulder joint
records.abstract: Background Mirror-based preoperative planning for total shoulder arthroplasty relies on accurate three-dimensional (3D) localization of bony landmarks on the contralateral, anatomically intact shoulder. Manual annotation is time-consuming and shows inter- and intra-observer variability. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a multi-task deep-learning network for automated 3D bony landmark detection on contralateral shoulder CT. Methods In this single-center retrospective study, 179 patients with intact contralateral shoulder CT scans were split at the patient level into training (n = 125), validation (n = 18), and test (n = 36) sets. We developed a dual-decoder 3D BiFormer-UNet for humerus and scapula segmentation and heatmap-based localization of 14 anatomical landmarks. A cross-task feature-fusion (CtFF) module transferred bone-structural guidance from the segmentation decoder to the landmark decoder. The network was trained end-to-end using a composite loss comprising hard-negative-mining heatmap regression, a geometric structure constraint, distance-aware similarity learning, and auxiliary segmentation loss. Landmark localization was evaluated using MRE and SDR at thresholds of 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, and 4.0 mm, while segmentation was assessed using the Dice coefficient. Per-case MRE was compared with four 3D baseline models using paired tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction. Results In the 36-case test set, the proposed model achieved an MRE of 2.1 ± 1.2 mm (95% CI, 1.7–2.5 mm) and SDRs of 72.0%, 81.8%, 90.3%, and 96.7% at thresholds of 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, and 4.0 mm, respectively. Its MRE was significantly lower than those of 3D U-Net, V-Net, 3D HRNet adaptation, and H3DE-Net (all Holm–Bonferroni-adjusted P < 0.05). On the test set, the auxiliary segmentation branch achieved mean Dice coefficients of 0.83 ± 0.05 for the humerus and 0.78 ± 0.07 for the scapula. Internally defined center landmarks, particularly the humeral head rotation center, anatomical neck center, and proximal and distal medullary canal centers, showed larger localization errors (2.3–2.6 mm) than most surface landmarks. Conclusion The proposed multi-task framework demonstrated promising 3D landmark localization performance on intact contralateral shoulder CT by integrating global anatomical context with bone-structural guidance. It may serve as an upstream localization component for mirror-based shoulder arthroplasty planning, although external validation is required before clinical use.

records.title: Interpretable and backpropagation-free Green Learning for efficient multi-task echocardiographic segmentation and classification
records.journal: APSIPA Transactions on Signal and Information Processing
records.abstract: Purpose This study develops an interpretable, backpropagation-free multi-task Green Learning (MTGL) framework for automated echocardiographic analysis. It addresses the need for reliable left ventricular (LV) segmentation and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) classification while reducing the parameter burden, energy demand and opacity associated with conventional deep learning (DL) models. The objective is to determine whether a unified feed-forward framework can deliver clinically relevant accuracy, computational efficiency and interpretable feature representations. Design/methodology/approach The framework uses a four-hop, PCA/Saab-based unsupervised VoxelHop encoder followed by a coarse-to-fine XGBoost residual-regression decoder for LV segmentation and a pooled multi-scale XGBoost classifier for three-class LVEF classification. Experiments used the predefined EchoNet-Dynamic training, validation and test partitions. MTGL was evaluated against matched 3D V-Net, 3D U-Net, 3D UNETR and 3D nnU-Net baselines using classification accuracy and balanced accuracy, and Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU). Findings On the EchoNet-Dynamic test set, MTGL achieved 94.3% accuracy for three-class LVEF classification, and 0.912 DSC for LV segmentation, outperforming all compared baselines. It used 1.13 million parameters, versus 10.47–49.08 million for the DL comparators, and showed the lowest measured training energy use and carbon emissions. Hop ablation further showed complementary multi-scale information, with the full feature set yielding the highest classification accuracy. Originality/value Unlike end-to-end backpropagation-based DL methods, MTGL combines an unsupervised linear VoxelHop representation with task-specific XGBoost decoders in a single multi-task echocardiographic pipeline. The PCA/Saab direct current and alternating current feature decomposition enables direct inspection of learned spatial and spatiotemporal signals, linking shallow features to anatomical boundaries and deeper features to global contractile dynamics. The study therefore demonstrates that a compact, interpretable Green Learning system can jointly support LV segmentation and LVEF grouping with strong in-domain performance and lower measured training environmental cost.

records.title: An explainable hybrid transformer–CNN framework for multi-class brain tumor classification from MRI images
records.abstract: Abstract The identification of brain tumors through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) requires effective methods that provide precise results because these results determine clinical choices. The study presents a classification system based on hybrid Transformer-CNN technology which classifies brain tumors into multiple types by using tumor segmentation and deep feature extraction and explainable artificial intelligence. The preprocessing of MRI images involves several steps which include skull stripping and CLAHE-based contrast enhancement and normalization and data augmentation and resizing to create high-quality images that maintain uniformity for model input. The TransUNet architecture performs tumor region segmentation by integrating convolutional neural networks with transformer-based attention systems which enable it to recognize both nearby and distant contextual details. The system generates segmentation masks which enable region-of-interest (ROI) feature extraction through DenseNet121 that has been pretrained on ImageNet while the final classification layer gets removed and global average pooling produces discriminative feature representations. The system uses an attention-based feature refinement method to improve feature representation followed by a regularized fully connected deep classifier which includes batch normalization and dropout for four-class classification of tumors. Model interpretability is achieved using Grad-CAM++ and attention visualization, enabling clear identification of tumor-related regions and improving model transparency. Experimental evaluation demonstrates high classification performance, achieving accuracies of 98.54% for meningioma, 98.65% for glioma, 99.45% for pituitary tumors, and 99.56% for no-tumor cases. These results indicate that presented TransUNet–DenseNet121 approach offers an accurate, reliable, interpretable method for detection of brain tumors automatically from MRI scanned images.

records.title: Quantitative Measurement of White Matter Hyperintensities in Brain MRI using a Multimodal Boundary-Aware Dual-Task Segmentation Framework
records.abstract: White matter hyperintensity (WMH) subtype segmentation in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains challenging due to heterogeneous lesion sizes, indistinct boundaries, and severe class imbalance. We propose a multimodal boundary-aware dual-task U-Net for segmenting periventricular (PVWMH), deep (DWMH), and subcortical (SWMH) lesions. The framework integrates FLAIR-T1-weighted feature fusion, Vision Mamba-based feature modeling, an SWMH-specific boundary loss, and auxiliary boundary detection. The method was evaluated using patient-level five-fold cross-validation on a private multicenter cohort (n = 75) and separately on 60 publicly annotated MICCAI WMH Challenge subjects for binary segmentation. On the private cohort, the proposed framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.6081 and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 14.80 mm, compared with 0.5638 and 18.25 mm for the FLAIR-only ablation baseline. It also improved SWMH DSC from 0.4610 with nnU-Net to 0.5215 (p = 0.008). On the public dataset, the mean binary DSC and HD95 were 0.6812 and 12.91 mm, respectively.Given the relatively large through-plane voxel spacing (8.4 mm), the framework processes 2D axial slices independently and does not explicitly model inter-slice context, which may limit its ability to characterize lesions extending across adjacent slices.

records.title: Comparative Analysis and Adaptation Strategies of Vision Foundation Models in Dermoscopic Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Accurate segmentation of skin lesions is of critical clinical importance for early melanoma diagnosis; however, the direct application of large foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to medical images characterized by low contrast and fuzzy boundaries remains insufficient due to substantial domain gaps. In current study, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy is presented by integrating lightweight adapter modules into a frozen Vision Transformer backbone. The proposed SAM-Adapter approach was comparatively evaluated against the original SAM and MedSAM models on the publicly available ISIC2018 and HAM10000 dermoscopic datasets. Optimized with AdamW, the model achieved the highest Dice (0.9603) and IoU (0.9241) scores along with the lowest HD95 (22.57) value on the HAM10000 dataset. Validated as statistically significant via the Wilcoxon test, this approach minimized computational overhead while demonstrating superior accuracy in boundary delineation. This adapter-based framework is planned for integration into clinical decision-support systems and other medical imaging modalities.

records.title: Automated segmentation and quantification of histological liver features for MASH/MASLD scoring
records.abstract: Abstract The increasing global prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) creates an urgent need for objective histopathological assessment. Conventional histological approaches are time-consuming and subjective. Therefore, we propose a fully automated, deep-learning-based pipeline for the segmentation and characterisation of histological liver features of MASH/MASLD. Segmentation was applied to H&E sections from 45 mice and 44 humans with MASH/MASLD. Our qHisto (quantitative histology) method, is nnU-Net-based and quantifies key histological components of the MASH-score, including steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation and ballooning. Additionally, we determined novel features that are inaccessible through manual histology, like the distribution of fat droplet sizes, nuclear aspect ratio and heatmaps. qHisto parameters showed strong positive correlations with conventional histology scores (fat: R = 0.91, inflammation: R = 0.70, ballooning: R = 0.47) and with hepatic fat fraction by magnetic resonance imaging ( R = 0.87). Our novel scores showed that nuclei deformation is driven by large fat droplets rather than the overall amount of fat. A key advantage of our method is spatially resolved, precise histological quantification to provide detailed assessment of disease severity. By automating time-consuming and repetitive readouts, qHisto improves standardisation and reproducibility of MASH/MASLD feature quantification and provides scalable, slide-wide analysis that supports histopathologists and enhances clinical assessment.
